title: KYE Evidence Pack
description: Self-contained, signed bundle that captures everything needed to replay and verify a single decision: a reference to the decision map, the immutable input blob, the signed state of the world used during evaluation, the supporting signals, signatures over the bundle, and a reference to the replay context seal. Auditors and regulators consume this as the unit of evidence.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Every runtime emitter stamps it and every canonical example carries it; pinned with const so the envelope cannot claim a schema it is not.

id.description: Stable URN of the evidence pack.

version.description: Schema major version. Pinned to 1 for kye.evidence.pack.v1.

decision_id.description: URN of the decision this pack provides evidence for.

decision_map_ref.description: Content-addressable reference to the kye.evidence.decision_map.v1 instance for this decision (e.g. its id or CID).

inputs_blob_ref.description: Content-addressable reference to the immutable, canonical-encoded inputs blob the engine consumed.

signed_state.description: Signed snapshot of the relevant state-of-the-world used during evaluation (grants in force, policies live, principal status, etc.).

state_hash.description: Hash over the canonical encoding of the state snapshot.

state_ref.description: Optional content-addressable reference to the full state snapshot blob.

signer.description: KYEID of the entity that signed the snapshot.

signals.description: External signals consumed during evaluation (risk scores, telemetry, attestations). Each carries provenance.

id.description: Locally-unique signal identifier inside the pack.

source.description: KYEID or URN of the signal producer.

payload_hash.description: Hash of the signal's canonical payload.

observed_at.description: Time the signal was observed by the engine.

signatures.description: Signatures binding the pack contents together (typically engine + principal countersignature).

replay_seal_ref.description: Content-addressable reference to the kye.replay.context_seal.v1 captured at decision time.

created_at.description: Time the evidence pack was assembled.

decided_in_region.description: §16 §12 Residency-proof (2026-06-10). The canonical residency region (kye:dictionary:data-residency region term) in which this decision was EVALUATED — the region-pinning PEP resolved the request and ran the policy here. Distinct from jurisdictions[] (legal jurisdiction): this is the infra deployment region. A regulator re-derives, from the pack alone, that the tenant's decision was made in-jurisdiction. Stamped by the region-pinning PEP (internal).

stored_in_region.description: §16 §12 Residency-proof (2026-06-10). The canonical residency region in which this evidence pack + decision record were PERSISTED (the region-pinned D1 + jurisdiction-restricted R2 bucket declared in internal). MUST equal decided_in_region unless the pack carries a cross_border record with a lawful_basis. A regulator re-derives that the evidence was stored in-jurisdiction.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions this evidence pack is scoped to — values from internal Used to filter regulator-facing replay: an ICO subpoena receives only UK-scoped packs; an OCR subpoena receives only US-scoped packs. The pack includes BOTH the data-subject jurisdiction and every processing-region the call touched, so cross-border calls surface their full route.

subject_jurisdiction_canonical.description: Jurisdiction of the data subject (where applicable) — drives lawful-basis selection + retention floor. Resolves against internal Optional in v1.x; required in v2.

cross_border.description: Cross-border transfer record. Populated automatically when subject_jurisdiction_canonical differs from any element of jurisdictions[] (i.e. the call crossed a boundary). Carries the lawful basis for the transfer so GDPR Art. 44-49 transfer-impact assessment is automatic.

lawful_basis.description: GDPR Art. 44-49 transfer mechanism. Mirrors EDPB Recommendations 01/2020.

basis_ref.description: URN or URL of the documentary evidence backing the lawful basis (e.g. SCC version, BCR approval reference).

memory_basis.description: §31 Memory Authority. Every agent-memory record the decision relied upon — as action evidence or as decision context — with the recall-time admissibility verdict. Empty/absent = the action relied on no memory. A regulator can re-derive whether the memory the agent acted on was authorised, current, scoped, consented and provenance-backed.

memory_id.description: URN of the kye.agent_memory.v1 record relied upon.

content_hash.description: Pins the exact memory version relied upon (matches kye.agent_memory.v1.content_hash).

used_as.description: Whether the memory was cited as evidence justifying the action, or only as background context informing it.

admissibility_state.description: Recall-time verdict (canonical enum — single declaration here). MEMORY_ADMISSIBLE/MEMORY_NOT_ADMISSIBLE are the terminal verdicts; the remainder are the reason states that drive them. A non-admissible memory used as action_evidence maps to the Action-Admissibility inadmissibility class `inadmissible_memory`.

reasons.description: Zero or more contributing reason states when admissibility_state is a terminal verdict (e.g. [MEMORY_STALE, MEMORY_SCOPE_EXCEEDED]).
